children: The newly introduced U.S. chip curbs will likely have limited impact on Tencent's artificial-intelligence business, Barclays analysts say in a note. Most of its AI agents don't require the highest-performing AI models, powered by the most advanced AI chips, they note. Users are quite happy with flash models, which carry highly economical price tags, they say. Tencent's ability to drive user adoption of its AI work assistant Workbuddy and monetize it is far more significant than having access to most advanced Nvidia chips, they note. Meanwhile, Tencent is on the verge of launching its AI agent for WeChat to all users in China as the costs of running the AI agent, Xiaowei, to support its 1.4 billion WeChat users have now become manageable. Tencent shares are 1.4% lower at 343.20 Hong Kong dollars. (sherry.qin@wsj.com)
